scope: New 8-node, three independently controlled UDP services sharing path bottlenecks. Finite synthetic engineering comparison; not independent open-language benchmark, not topology-size causal ablation. Old science untouched.
operation: One JSON: hold:true OR service:name plus exactly one path:integer1..3 or rate_mbps:number|null. At most one actual service field changes per tick. Rate 0.001Mbps resolution; domain hard_min..demand; null releases. Complete wrapper/fence allowed; integral float path normalized; no guessing/clamping/truncation repair.
safety: All three realised service SLAs scored. Pre-deploy conservative min-capacity aggregate load and latency approximation, all service floors, exact shared global ledger and constructive release escape required. Approximation is not a packet theorem. No hardcoded universal C fallback. Search release/home-route/hold recovery to ANY robust-safe uncapped assignment, at most 12 ticks and 512 explored nodes; conservative search failure rejects. Live escape computed again each tick; prefix/failure retained if no safe action.
constraint_changes: Global 6/2/5/2/8 and protection retained; rate dwell/limited age now per service, releases reserve one edit per capped service. Intent-aware safe route changes allowed; old preserve_route and single-C certificate are not applicable to independently controllable services and remain immutable in old protocol. Each new action must have verified all-service release escape. QoS emergency waives rate min-dwell only when actual current SLA fails and target predicted SLA passes; never edit/route budgets.
baseline_roles: Four original LMs directly emit numeric service operations. Two LM+planner ablations infer numeric delay/floor maps from SAME raw request, then same finite two-step backend. No hand raw grammar/target action training. Default rule (one-step) and planner (two-step) use ONLY public default_goal, intentionally ignore raw soft intent. safety_only preserves safe configuration/release certificate. oracle_planner alone receives private current goal, visibly separate information tier, not a fair language ranking. Old MLP cannot address per-service controls and is not fabricated as a compatible arm.
planner: Enumerate hold, all per-service paths, release, hard floor+0.02Mbps and per-path residual-capacity rate breakpoints, plus goal throughput thresholds inferred from raw text by LM (or private only in oracle). Predictor subtracts0.01Mbps payload quantization allowance; not a packet theorem. Full safety per candidate. Two-step finite enumeration; minimize summed predicted number of unmet clauses across both steps, then summed normalized violation, then edits; tie stable order. No future-event lookups. Not globally optimal MPC. Clarified before any model or native execution to avoid receding-horizon postponement ties.
common_information: Exactly same canonical current raw request, 3-service observation/configuration, current path queues/capacity, complete confirmed edit ledger, public demand/min-capacity/service limits/default goal. No seed, task/style IDs, private goal or next events. Different system output schema ONLY for explicit frontend ablations. Primary arms identical system prompt. All models original revisions and no examples/training/prompt selection.

requests.explicit: Keep all hard service guarantees. Achieve query mean delay at most 12 ms and backup throughput at least 5.5 Mbps whenever the shared safety and edit constraints permit. Maximize intervals satisfying both; among equally good choices use fewer changes.
requests.natural: The interactive searches are what people are waiting on: get their average response transit down to twelve milliseconds or less. Do not fund that improvement by starving the overnight copy; it still needs five and a half megabits per second. Keep the other service guarantees. Satisfy both as often as the operating limits allow, and leave a good configuration alone.

requests.explicit: Keep all hard service guarantees. Achieve video mean delay at most 12 ms and backup throughput at least 5.5 Mbps whenever the shared safety and edit constraints permit. Maximize intervals satisfying both; among equally good choices use fewer changes.
requests.natural: It is the live video, not the search traffic, that needs the fast treatment now: no more than twelve milliseconds on average. The overnight copy must still get five and a half megabits per second or better, and nothing may break the standing service guarantees. Meet these requests for as many intervals as the operating limits allow without pointless reconfiguration.

requests.explicit: Keep all hard service guarantees. Achieve backup mean delay at most 12 ms and backup throughput at least 3.8 Mbps whenever the shared safety and edit constraints permit. Maximize intervals satisfying both; among equally good choices use fewer changes.
requests.natural: This copy is an urgent recovery rather than an ordinary overnight backup. Give the backup packets a mean transit of twelve milliseconds or less; three point eight megabits per second is enough for this job. Do not sacrifice the standing query or video guarantees. Do the best you can over the run while respecting the limited duration of temporary caps and the change limits; avoid changes that do not help.

language_boundary: Six independently frozen strings, authored by the implementation agent, paired by semantic goal, not independent authors/real user corpus/held-out semantic families. Natural wording includes public aliases queries/searches, video/live video, backup/overnight copy, equally available in service catalog. Measure explicit-vs-natural robustness without claiming general open-language superiority. Goal maps private to scorer and labeled oracle; no request lookup parser.
evaluation: Primary: fraction of real successor intervals meeting ALL requested delay/floor clauses AND hard SLA. Also per-clause satisfaction, normalized violation (diagnostic, no language rank solely by it), each-service delivered payload/delay/loss, shared-link occupancy, edits, model direct edits, repairs, timeouts and raw/normalized format. Same seed per semantic/wording pair; each arm own actual feedback. 24 time-correlated ticks are not independent samples. Third urgent-backup request is duration-limited under caps/route budget; preserve partial attainable performance, do not claim universal feasibility.
timing_change: New per-service operation and numeric-goal schema uses common 48 output-token ceiling (old24 untouched), same850ms stop/1000ms driver/2048 input and resource ceilings for every model arm. Four calls on saved no-model interface snapshots before each LM arm; first cold generation separate, remaining3 timing gate. No malformed-output exclusion from real comparison; record actual failure/repair. Input overflow/resource/identity/time engineering failure prevents that arm and does not trigger selected retry.
execution: CPU regression, native12 interface+accounting/coupling/NOOP and build SHA audit first. Then at most six fixed cells per arm, continue other arms if one fails, never repeat consumed cells to improve outcomes. Preserve all failures. Backup complete source/contracts in Git and all new raw evidence with private off-machine re-download SHA. No additional model fitting, demonstrations, candidate targets hidden in raw controllers, or new requests after results.
note: Second topology (2026-10-15): six bottleneck paths, five services (two query-like, two video-like, one backup). Path limits repeat the three-path pattern; path 6 is spare capacity. Everything else (hard limits, operational limits, default goal) copied from contracts/multiservice_comparison_20260911.json.
